claims.quote: The cab was still flying at an even speed in a great circle and Ralph saw that it was imperative that he get control of it at once, for another machine, bound evidently for New York, was bearing down upon the helpless men.
claims.description: Flying aerocabs serve as everyday taxis along crowded airways.

claims.quote: Ralph had immediately transmitted the lost girl's photograph to the Central Office where it was placed before a Telephot connecting with every member of the entire police force
claims.description: A video telephone network lets photographs be transmitted instantly to the whole police force.

claims.quote: the picture was reproduced for them in their portable radio instruments for ten seconds
claims.description: Police carry portable radio instruments that display images.

claims.quote: A multitude of inventions and suggestions were made, but none proved to be of any value until the *Anti-Gravitator* was invented by the American 969L 9 in the year 2210.
claims.description: A gyroscope-based anti-gravity device is invented to lift vehicles off the Earth.

claims.quote: it became possible to lift a weight of 1,000 kilograms with an anti-gravitator weighing but 12 kilograms.
claims.description: Anti-gravity units lift 1,000 kg with a 12 kg device.

claims.quote: Towards the end of the twenty-first century, when atmospheric flying had become common, scientists began seriously to think of constructing machinery to enable man to leave the confines of the planet to which humanity had been chained for ages.
claims.description: Atmospheric flying becomes common by the end of the twenty-first century and spaceflight follows.
claims.stated_time: towards the end of the twenty-first century

claims.quote: the enormous population of Earth, which had passed the twelve billion mark, clamored for an adequate outlet which the planet itself could no longer furnish.
claims.description: Earth's population exceeds twelve billion and drives demand for space colonization.

claims.quote: A *pulsating polarized ether wave*, if directed on a metal object can be reflected in the same manner as a light-ray is reflected from a bright surface or from a mirror.
claims.description: A radar-like system bounces waves off metal objects in space to determine their location and distance.

claims.quote: The manufacturer also told him that the entire outside shell was of *Magnelium*—an invention of Ralph's—and that this flyer was the first to be equipped with the new metal.
claims.description: A new metal alloy is invented for spacecraft hulls.

claims.quote: Ralph's machine had made 80,000 miles an hour since its start.
claims.description: Spacecraft travel at tens of thousands of miles per hour.

claims.quote: Thus any object, regardless of its earthly weight, *hung freely suspended in the center of the space flyer*.
claims.description: Objects become weightless inside a spacecraft and float.

claims.quote: *Sleep was practically impossible.*
claims.description: Spacefarers are unable to sleep properly in space.

claims.quote: the original supply taken from the earth is used over and over by altering the carbonic acid gas by means of automatic generators.
claims.description: Spacecraft recycle air by chemically converting carbon dioxide.

claims.quote: In a few minutes he anchored his flyer to the other by means of a powerful electromagnet.
claims.description: Two spacecraft dock in flight using an electromagnet and an airtight connecting tube.

claims.quote: Ralph had struck him senseless with his *Radioperforer*.
claims.description: A ray weapon that knocks a person unconscious through a spacecraft window.

claims.quote: I pricked his hand with a little *Catalepsol*. In fifteen minutes he will be all right again.
claims.description: A drug induces temporary rigid paralysis and recovers after fifteen minutes.

claims.quote: As all space flyers must be licensed by law, he had no trouble in getting the information he desired.
claims.description: Spacecraft are licensed and registered by law, and the registry can be queried by telephone.

claims.quote: As Planet Governor it is my duty to advise you that you have not the right to place your person in unnecessary danger.
claims.description: A planetary government with a Planet Governor can forbid scientists from risking their lives.

claims.quote: Surely, not to Venus where the inhabitants were nearly all Terrestrials, and whose laws were identical with those of Earth.
claims.description: Humans have colonized Venus under Earth's laws.

claims.quote: He knew enough of the Martian character to realize that Alice was in the hands of a man who, once the die was cast, would stop at nothing.
claims.description: Intelligent Martians exist and interact with humans.
